page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 4.0 GB per core ratio. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. This configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Local storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieves a top-tier score of 3135.87, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Geekbench single-core performance is also strong at 2147.0, ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core and parallel processing benchmarks show limitations; the Geekbench multi-core score of 3829.0 and the stress-ng multi-core score of 6213.65 fall into the weak and average categories, respectively. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with small-block cached reads performing in the bottom 25% at 298.13 GB/sec, while large-block uncached reads and writes achieve average tier results of 71.86 GB/sec and 53.72 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits performance bottlenecks in database operations and high-throughput web serving. Passmark database operations scored in the bottom 10% at 1074.47, and static web serving throughput was similarly limited at 2.26 GB/sec. Redis SET operations also registered in the bottom 25% with 4.8 million operations per second. Qualitatively, the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance offer stable compute resources for workloads that do not require massive parallelization. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, and basic development environments rather than high-concurrency databases or intensive web serving.
